methods.reasonPercent: Per-second sampled-frame count divided by captured sample count; not all 100 ms decisions and not causal time attribution. escape/cap200-finish are kept separately.
methods.eligibleNpc: Planner meals classified edible before target reachability/utility selection; includes more than the chosen target. Zero does not prove no truly edible NPC existed.
methods.flatHud: Consecutive one-second samples with identical rounded displayed HUD. Duration is last minus first timestamp; eating below HUD rounding can occur.
methods.npcPursuit: Consecutive samples with intercept-growth reason and a local body NPC target; target IDs/positions are not saved, so this does not prove pursuit of the same NPC.
methods.geometry: Only selected-target radius and visualR are saved. Silhouette wobble is real; r/visualR disagreement is not proof of physical-radius error. No pixels, persistent IDs, or original/highlight centres are present, so neither per-NPC radius instability nor geometry acceptance/correction rate can be reconstructed.
methods.growthWindows: Overlapping observational windows, not independent trials or NPC swallow rates. Any HUD increase may come from food/other NPC.
methods.scope: Five completed Grow-14 starts only; sixth partial reported separately. No Grow-15 gameplay inference.

partial.limitations: Sparse approximately 5-second progress latest samples cannot establish a continuous plateau or final outcome. Parent observed later live HUD separately; this JSON uses saved events only.

aggregateGeometryObservation.interpretation: Disagreement can arise from intentional silhouette wobble; selected-target-only data cannot estimate global radius error or geometry acceptance. Geometry applies after NPC classification and existing component filters, so it does not directly fix NPCs omitted or classified as food.

findings.statement: Run04 has the most zero-eligible samples (68.2%), but losing run05 has the highest average eligible NPC count (1.48) and lowest zero fraction (28.7%). Low eligible count cannot explain all losses.

Run05 HUD remains125 from98 through111s;101 through110s are consecutive intercept-growth samples. Winning run03 also has HUD30 plateau5 through15s entirely in intercept-growth, so a plateau is not sufficient to predict failure.

No stable target ID or x/y is retained in one-second samples. Per-NPC radius instability, exact target switches, true swallow misses and causal attribution to radius or planning cannot be established.
Geometry could improve accepted detected-NPC centre/radius estimates; actual acceptance, tick cost and any outcome effect require the frozen Grow15 test. Synthetic passing is not gameplay evidence.
